chapter: Memphis, Oklahoma, the Kirk band and Kansas City
title: How the Kirk band rehearsed and its range of styles
summary: The band made arrangements on the spot, played for white and black dances, could sound like Guy Lombardo or Basie, and its musicians inspired her to start arranging.

story.theme_name: Writing and arranging: how musicians compose
story.community_name: Writing, arranging and composing: how the music gets made

blocks.x: How had T. Holder managed to get this group together, especially...?

I really don't know. I never did find out but it was something really special. Claude Williams had played the violin and he was terrific. This was the most wonderful thing how they rehearsed. They'd call a rehearsal and nobody would prepare an arrangement. They'd do it while they were there. In one corner somebody would be playing cards or talking or something and Andy would say, "O.K.,

rhythm section first." And after that the trumpets and the saxophones. In this particular band they had a guy that played - they called him like a clown. He did all the acrobatics and everything on his back with this tenor and all that. They had other musicians that were real true musicians and what I did when I began writing, I'd teach this guy how to phrase with them because he was a little corny - the one that was doing all the tricks while he was playing. They did little acts and they did everything. They could play like Guy Lombardo and they could swing like Count Basie. It was the most amazing band I've ever been with in my life. They could play so many different styles and this put them in the category of Guy Lombardo. They could play for proms and everything and then go to an all black dance and be just as good, you know, swinging.
They worked a lot of white dates?

Yes, they did more white dates than anything else. Then when we first began to hit in the 30's everyone thought Andy was white because they had never seen a picture of him, because the band sounded like it on some things that we played. He believed in phrasing ballads in a very beautiful way, like violins. This band, they had a way of getting arrangements and things on the spot. During that era we didn't have great readers among black musicians and these guys could read anything. Like the first trumpet had such a sound, Big Jim Lawson, he was terrific.

Maybe the other two trumpets or one trumpet sound wasn't as big and he just covered the entire band sometimes when we didn't have everybody with a good sound. It was a most enjoyable thing after I joined them. It was exciting and I think they are really the reasons that I began to arrange.
